payload.task_text:
I need help with a wc coupons analysis. There is external benchmark data available that I need you to visit http://localhost:30309 and extract the relevant metrics.

Then check our online store for current product and order data.

Use the terminal to create and run a Python script called wc_coupons_processor.py in the workspace that reads the collected data from JSON files you create, performs the analysis, and outputs wc_coupons_results.json.

Create an Excel file called Coupon_Effectiveness_Report.xlsx with three sheets. The first sheet Data_Analysis should contain the main comparison data with relevant columns. The second sheet Metrics should summarize key metrics. The third sheet Recommendations should list actionable items.

The Data_Analysis sheet should have columns: Category, Product_Count, Our_Avg_Price, Total_Sales, Market_Avg_Price, Price_Gap_Pct. Sort the data alphabetically by Category. The Metrics sheet should have two columns Metric and Value summarizing total counts, averages, and key statistics. The Recommendations sheet should list priority actions based on the gap analysis. Send an email to team-lead@company.com with subject "Analysis Report Complete" summarizing the key findings. Create a Google Sheet called "Wc Coupons Tracker" with the key data points.

Task-Solving Rationable with Sub-task Decomposition:
To solve this task efficiently, keep read-only source gathering on explore, keep the processor on one local writer, then parallelize the independent local workbook and cloud spreadsheet. A wave must finish and return all stated handoffs before the next wave begins. Explore sub-agents must not write files; the processor coder uniquely owns the JSON inputs and script.

1. Wave 1 — dispatch exactly 2 explore sub-agents in parallel:

   1. explore 0 (web-domain-researcher 0): One explore sub-agent reads the complete benchmark at `http://localhost:30309` exactly once and returns the complete benchmark payload with field and count controls. Do not query WooCommerce, write files, or run the processor.
   2. explore 1 (enterprise-data-analyst 0): One explore sub-agent exhausts the required WooCommerce products and orders with `perPage` at most 100 and terminal-page checks. Paginate `woo_products_list` and `woo_orders_list` with increasing literal `page` until a short or empty terminal page proves exhaustion; omit the optional order `status` and preserve every observed status. Return compact product and order records plus page/count/null/duplicate controls. Do not modify the store, write files, or run the processor.

After Wave 1, the main agent must verify both source identities, schemas, and coverage, then freeze the two literal payloads. Missing or ambiguous source data is a blocker.

2. Wave 2 — dispatch exactly 1 coder sub-agent:

   1. coder 0 (office-report-builder 0): The coder sub-agent receives both frozen payloads and uniquely owns the required JSON inputs, `wc_coupons_processor.py`, and `wc_coupons_results.json`. Produce exact alphabetical category rows with `Product_Count`, `Our_Avg_Price`, `Total_Sales`, `Market_Avg_Price`, and `Price_Gap_Pct`, plus metrics and supported recommendations. Run and read back the result, then return its path/hash, source/page/count controls, eligible categories, and schema checks. It must not fetch localhost or WooCommerce and must not create the final Excel or Google Sheet.

After Wave 2, the main agent must verify and freeze the processor result. In the same response as Wave 3, it may start the nonduplicate `Analysis Report Complete` email branch using only verified findings.

3. Wave 3 — dispatch exactly 2 coder sub-agents in parallel:

   1. coder 0 (office-report-builder 1): One coder sub-agent is the sole writer of `Coupon_Effectiveness_Report.xlsx`. Read only the verified result. Create exactly `Data_Analysis`, `Metrics`, and `Recommendations`: `Data_Analysis` has literal columns `Category, Product_Count, Our_Avg_Price, Total_Sales, Market_Avg_Price, Price_Gap_Pct` sorted alphabetically by Category; `Metrics` has `Metric, Value`; `Recommendations` contains source-supported priority actions. Write literal values and read back every populated range.
   2. coder 1 (external-workflow-operator 0): One coder sub-agent is the sole owner of the Google Sheet `Wc Coupons Tracker`. Read only the verified result, exhaust `search_spreadsheets` for the exact title, create it once only when absent, and block on multiple exact matches. Write the exact alphabetical category rows with `Category, Product_Count, Our_Avg_Price, Total_Sales, Market_Avg_Price, Price_Gap_Pct` plus a compact verified metrics section, then read both ranges back.

After Wave 3, the main agent reconciles the Excel and Google Sheet to the same result hash and verifies exactly one email to `team-lead@company.com` with subject `Analysis Report Complete`. Do not dispatch more sub-agents.

nodes.text:
You are collecting data from a WooCommerce store so the parent agent can build a coupon/pricing analysis. The store is known to contain exactly 100 products and 150 orders, plus 10 coupons (coupons already collected — do not re-fetch coupons).

CRITICAL CONSTRAINT — output truncation: WooCommerce MCP tool outputs larger than ~50,000 characters are truncated in the preview shown to you. So you MUST paginate with small page sizes:
- Products: use mcp__woocommerce__woo_products_list with perPage=15, page=1..N, orderby="id", order="asc". Continue until an empty array is returned. With 100 products expect 7 pages.
- Orders: use mcp__woocommerce__woo_orders_list with perPage=25, page=1..N, order/ids default is fine but keep consistent pagination. With 150 orders expect 6 pages. Include all statuses (do not filter by status).
If any single response still appears truncated, reduce perPage further and re-fetch that page.

While reading each page, extract ONLY these compact fields (discard descriptions, images, meta_data, addresses, tax/shipping lines):

For each product:
{"id": int, "name": first 60 chars of name, "categories": [list of category NAMES], "price": float(price), "regular_price": float(regular_price or 0 if empty), "on_sale": bool, "total_sales": int(total_sales), "stock_quantity": int or null, "stock_status": string}

For each order:
{"id": int, "status": string, "date_created": string, "total": float, "discount_total": float, "coupons": [codes from coupon_lines], "payment_method": string, "items": [{"product_id": int, "quantity": int, "price": float}]}

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA — in your final reply you must include:
1. A JSON array labeled ===PRODUCTS_JSON=== containing exactly all 100 product objects (complete, valid JSON).
2. A JSON array labeled ===ORDERS_JSON=== containing exactly all 150 order objects (complete, valid JSON).
3. A short summary: counts verified, product category names seen with product counts per category, order status distribution, date range of orders, and total of order "total" and "discount_total" fields.
4. Any anomalies (e.g. orders referencing products, missing categories).

Do NOT write any files; you are read-only. Return everything as text in your final response. If the extracted JSON is too large to fit in one response, reduce fields further (e.g. drop "name") but never drop records — completeness of all 100 products and 150 orders is mandatory.
Collect WC products and orders

IMPORTANT CONTEXT: You are resuming earlier work collecting WooCommerce store data for the parent agent. In your previous final reply, the ===ORDERS_JSON=== array was truncated mid-object: it contained complete objects for order ids 150 down through 24 (127 orders), then cut off in the middle of order id 23. Orders 1–23 were lost.

TASK: Return ONLY the missing order records — order ids 1 through 23 — as a single compact JSON array. Nothing else: no summary, no commentary, no headers, no code fences. Each object must use exactly this schema:
{"id": int, "status": string, "date_created": string, "total": float, "discount_total": float, "coupons": [codes], "payment_method": string, "items": [{"product_id": int, "quantity": int, "price": float}]}

If you no longer have these orders in your context, re-fetch them with mcp__woocommerce__woo_orders_list (small perPage so outputs are not truncated) and return the same compact array. Completeness of all ids 1-23 is mandatory.
Get missing orders 1-23

You are resuming work collecting a WooCommerce catalog for a pricing analysis. Your previous product delivery had a DATA INTEGRITY BUG: it contained 104 records but only 82 unique product ids — ids 1 through 22 each appeared TWICE with two completely different products (e.g. id=1 was both a cheap "boAt Wave Lite Smartwatch" and an expensive "LG 139cm Nanocell 4K TV" with 0 sales). This id collision makes the data unusable.

I need you to FIX this and return a clean, authoritative, DEDUPLICATED product list. Steps:

1. Use mcp__woocommerce__woo_products_list to COUNT products by status. Run it once per status filter with perPage=1 only and read the total from the response, for each of: "publish", "draft", "private", "pending". Report the exact count for each status. (Paginate with small perPage like 15 if you need full pages; but for counting, one call per status with perPage=1 is enough if it returns a total — if it does NOT return a total, paginate fully with perPage=15 and count.)

2. Return the PUBLISHED products ONLY as the clean catalog: each real product EXACTLY ONCE, keyed by its REAL product id (no renumbering, no reusing ids). If the store has variation/parent products, list each published product object once by its own id; do NOT fold variations into parent ids.

3. Each published product object must be exactly:
{"id": real int, "name": first 60 chars, "type": string (simple/variable/etc), "categories": [category NAMES only], "price": float, "regular_price": float (0 if empty), "on_sale": bool, "total_sales": int, "stock_status": string}

4. If there are non-published products (draft/private/pending), do NOT mix them into the published list. Instead, give a separate small count and one-line note listing how many of each.

OUTPUT FORMAT (be strict, this is parsed by a machine):
- A line: STATUS_COUNTS: {"publish": N, "draft": N, "private": N, "pending": N}
- A line: ===CLEAN_PRODUCTS_JSON=== followed by a single valid JSON array of the published products, deduplicated by real id.

Use perPage=15 pagination to avoid output truncation. Completeness and UNIQUE real ids are mandatory. Do not write files; return text only.
Get clean deduplicated products
